item.title: All Latin Songs & Albums Inducted Into the National Recording Registry
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we celebrate the rich diversity of music that shapes the American landscape. Today, we're shining the spotlight on Latin music and its incredible contributions to the American songbook. From Celia Cruz to Daddy Yankee, Latin artists have been making waves in the music industry for decades."
[Short music clip: "Gasolina" by Daddy Yankee]
Host: "The Library of Congress' National Recording Registry is dedicated to preserving sound recordings that are culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant to American life. And this year, two more Latin songs have been added to the registry: José Feliciano's 'Feliz Navidad' and Pérez Prado and His Orchestra's 'Mambo No. 5'."
[Short music clip: "Feliz Navidad" by José Feliciano]
Host: "These additions join a growing list of Latin music legends, including Vicente Fernández, Freddy Fender, and Tito Puente. In fact, over 20 works of Latin music have been included in the registry since its creation in 2000."
[Short music clip: "La Bamba" by Ritchie Valens]
Host: "Other notable inductees include Santana's 'Abraxas', Buena Vista Social Club's self-titled album, and Ritchie Valens' iconic 'La Bamba'. These songs represent the vibrant and diverse contributions of Latin artists to American music."
[Short music clip: "Mambo No. 5" by Pérez Prado and His Orchestra]
Host: "As Congressman Joaquin Castro notes, having a song inducted into the National Recording Registry is a prestigious honor, not just for Latin artists, but for all musicians. And with Latin music continuing to shape the American landscape, we can expect to see many more incredible additions to the registry in the years to come."
[Outro music plays]
Host: "Thanks for joining us on this journey through the world of Latin music. Join us next time as we explore more of the amazing stories and sounds that make up the American musical heritage."
